gutter_arrival.speaker: narrator
gutter_arrival.text: The Gutter. The deep fold where the pages meet. Every drop of the flood had run down here in the end, and it had nowhere left to go.

gutter_arrival.speaker: patch
gutter_arrival.text: ...Okay. Okay. No sidekicks. That's fine. Classic hero stuff. The lone fox walks into the dark.

gutter_arrival.speaker: patch
gutter_arrival.text: The lone fox would really like a torch, though.

gutter_arrival.speaker: patch
gutter_arrival.text: Right. The Sogg came down here, so there's only one way to go. Down and along. Story of my life, lately.

gutter_echoes.speaker: narrator
gutter_echoes.text: The water down here remembered everything it had soaked. Shapes kept rising out of it.

gutter_echoes.speaker: patch
gutter_echoes.text: Every Soggy in the book must drain down here. Brilliant. It's like the world's worst bath.

gutter_sogg_arrival.speaker: sogg
gutter_sogg_arrival.text: You came down on your own. Your friends are up on the spine. Nobody's coming.

gutter_sogg_arrival.speaker: patch
gutter_sogg_arrival.text: I noticed. I'm doing great, thanks for asking.

gutter_sogg_arrival.speaker: sogg
gutter_sogg_arrival.text: Do you know what this place is, fox? It's where everything ends up. Every word that ran. Every page that wouldn't dry.

gutter_sogg_arrival.speaker: sogg
gutter_sogg_arrival.text: Nobody fixes the middle of a book. They just close it.

gutter_sogg_arrival.speaker: patch
gutter_sogg_arrival.text: Then I'll fix it. I've been told I'm very annoying about things like that.

gutter_losing.speaker: patch
gutter_losing.text: ...I can't. I can't get a hit in. The folds won't even stand up.

gutter_losing.speaker: sogg
gutter_losing.text: Of course not. Down here, everything goes soft. You can stop now.

gutter_losing.speaker: patch
gutter_losing.text: Dot was right, you know. Everybody tears.

gutter_losing.speaker: patch
gutter_losing.text: ...Maybe. Maybe I just can't do this one on my own.

gutter_losing.speaker: narrator
gutter_losing.text: The Sogg closed over him like a wet blanket. Everything went dark and cold and heavy.

gutter_losing.speaker: narrator
gutter_losing.text: And then, far above, at the very edge of the page, a light came on.

warm_air_arrives.speaker: narrator
warm_air_arrives.text: Something came down out of the Margin into the Gutter: a huge pink nozzle, humming, and with it, a wind as warm as an oven door.

warm_air_arrives.speaker: patch
warm_air_arrives.text: The Great Light has... a weather? Since when does the Great Light have a weather?

warm_air_arrives.speaker: sogg
warm_air_arrives.text: No. No! Turn it off. NOT WARM!

warm_air_arrives.speaker: patch
warm_air_arrives.text: Oh, you don't like that at all, do you.

warm_air_arrives.speaker: patch
warm_air_arrives.text: Okay. Somebody out there is on my side. Let's go, Sogg. Round two.

drizzle_dried.speaker: narrator
drizzle_dried.text: The Sogg shrank, and shrank, until all that was left was a small white cloud, about the size of a fox, looking at the floor.

drizzle_dried.speaker: drizzle
drizzle_dried.text: I'm really sorry. About the whole... drowning everything. And the dragging. And the, um. Monologues.

drizzle_dried.speaker: patch
drizzle_dried.text: The monologues were a lot, yeah.

drizzle_dried.speaker: drizzle
drizzle_dried.text: When the flood came, I soaked up so much of it. I kept getting heavier, and nobody could see me any more, just the wet. I thought, if I'm ruined, then everything should be.

drizzle_dried.speaker: drizzle
drizzle_dried.text: That way I wouldn't be the only one.

drizzle_dried.speaker: patch
drizzle_dried.text: ...Yeah. I get that. When the water came, I ran. I spent three chapters telling everyone a thunderstorm did it.

drizzle_dried.speaker: patch
drizzle_dried.text: No. A sheep saw. Then I told the truth, and it turned out my friends had tape on them too. Loads of it.

drizzle_dried.speaker: patch
drizzle_dried.text: Everybody tears. Period. Somebody clever told me that.

drizzle_dried.speaker: drizzle
drizzle_dried.text: ...Can I still be the Weather Page's rain? Just a bit of rain. Light. Occasional.

drizzle_dried.speaker: patch
drizzle_dried.text: I think the meadow would like that. Come on. Let's go up. It's warm up there now.

interlude_4.speaker: narrator
interlude_4.text: Two in the morning. Dad was still asleep at the table. Nell had come down for a glass of water and hadn't gone back up.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: Old ladies don't sleep, love. We just wait for the kettle.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: Look at the middle of the book. It's still soaked. It's worse than yesterday. The fox's page is just... empty.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: Dad's going to wake up and try to fix it and it's not going to work, and he'll just keep trying anyway.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: He will. He's like that. So was your grandad.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: Nell. Mended isn't the same as broken. People think it's halfway back to new. It isn't. It's its own thing.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: My mug's got three glue lines. It holds tea better than it ever did, because I'm careful with it now. That's what the glue's for. Not to hide the crack. To show you cared enough to fix it.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: That's such a Gran thing to say.

interlude_4.speaker: gran
interlude_4.text: Thank you. I've been saving it.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: ...The plug's right next to the book. I'd have sworn it was over by the sink.

interlude_4.speaker: narrator
interlude_4.text: Nell plugged the hairdryer in, switched it to warm, and pointed it at the very middle of the book.

interlude_4.speaker: nell
interlude_4.text: Okay, fox. Hang on. I'm coming.

ending_table.speaker: narrator
ending_table.text: Morning. Sun came through the laundromat steam and across Gran's table.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: Nell? Did you... You dried the Gutter.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: Somebody had to. You were snoring on the winter page.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: The middle's dry. It's all dry. It's lumpy. It's a bit warped. But it's...

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: I think I like it anyway.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: Dad, the envelope. 'Patch, tail.' Can we put it back on?

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: I tried. It's just pulp now, love. The ink ran right through it.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: Then we make him a new one. Hang on.

ending_table.speaker: narrator
ending_table.text: Nell cut a strip from the Lanternfold harbour map, the corner that had never quite dried right, and folded it into a tail.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: Tape on the inside, so it doesn't show?

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: No. On the outside. So he can see it.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: And there's a blank page at the back. It's been blank since I was born.

ending_table.speaker: dad
ending_table.text: I never knew what to put there.

ending_table.speaker: nell
ending_table.text: I do. Pass me the crayons.

ending_table.speaker: narrator
ending_table.text: Dad laughed. Gran laughed. Nell told them to stop watching her draw, and then she laughed too.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: Whoa. This page is new. It smells like crayon.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: dot
epilogue_arrival.text: Patch! You're alive. You're dry. You're... what's that on your back?

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: Oh, this? Funny story. I fought a thunderstorm and...

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: Okay, okay. Somebody made it for me. It's a bit of the harbour map, and it's taped on, and the tape shows. On purpose.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: corrugate
epilogue_arrival.text: Suits you, fox. A tail with a map on it. Now you'll always know where you've been.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: dot
epilogue_arrival.text: Everyone's here. Go and say hello. Then it's the end of the book.

epilogue_arrival.speaker: patch
epilogue_arrival.text: The end? Already? I was just getting good at this.

epilogue_drizzle.speaker: drizzle
epilogue_drizzle.text: Everyone keeps being nice to me. It's very confusing.

epilogue_drizzle.speaker: drizzle
epilogue_drizzle.text: Shepherd Fluff asked if I could do a light shower on Thursdays. For the grass. I said yes. I've never been booked before.

epilogue_bindwell.speaker: bindwell
epilogue_bindwell.text: The spine's restrung. Proper kettle stitch, all the way down. It'll hold another hundred years.

epilogue_bindwell.speaker: bindwell
epilogue_bindwell.text: Mind you, so will that tail of yours. That's good tape, that. Real-world tape. Wear it with your chin up.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: shepherd_fluff
epilogue_fluff.text: Well, look at you. A tail again.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: patch
epilogue_fluff.text: You can tell everyone the real story, by the way. The running away bit. I don't mind.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: shepherd_fluff
epilogue_fluff.text: Already did, lad. Years ago. Well. Two chapters ago. Nobody thought less of you.

epilogue_fluff.speaker: shepherd_fluff
epilogue_fluff.text: Sheep don't care about tails. We care who comes back for us. You did.

epilogue_lamplighters.speaker: lamplighters
epilogue_lamplighters.text: The festival's back on! Tonight! On this page, because it's the only one that's properly dry.

epilogue_lamplighters.speaker: lamplighters
epilogue_lamplighters.text: Bring the cloud. She can do the misty bit over the lanterns. It'll be gorgeous.

the_end.speaker: narrator
the_end.text: On the last page of the book, under Dad's old handwriting, there was a new line, in crayon.

the_end.speaker: nell_hand
the_end.text: THE POP-UP KINGDOM OF FOLDWICK. Soaked, torn, dried, taped, and finished.

the_end.speaker: nell_hand
the_end.text: Made by Dad. Mended by Dad, Gran, and Nell. And a fox.
